evidence: createApp registers Express routes that each call a CatalogueService or OrderService method (for example orders.placeOrder(command) and catalogue.restock(...)): transport routing only.
asObject, requireString, requireNumber and param only check the type and shape of request input, which is transport-level validation.
errorHandler and statusFor turn DomainError subclasses into HTTP status codes and JSON error bodies, which is an HTTP adapter's job.
app.post('/orders/:id/pay', ...) and similar routes pass a fixed target state to orders.transition. Whether the transition is allowed is decided outside this file.
The /stock route only maps fields from listProducts() into a response view. It does not calculate stock rules.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http.ts is an Express transport adapter, and all of its responsibilities belong in infrastructure. It sets up routes, checks the shape of JSON input (asObject, requireString, requireNumber, param), maps domain errors to HTTP status codes and response bodies (errorHandler, statusFor), and handles a malformed-body error that is specific to Express (isBodyParseError). The file has no business rules: placing orders, restocking, order state changes, the advance logic and cancellation are all passed to the application services. The /stock projection only reshapes data for the response. The /orders/:id/pay, /pack, /ship and /deliver endpoints only map each URL to a target state; the transition rules stay in OrderService and the domain. The state checks reuse the domain's isOrderState and ORDER_STATES instead of re-implementing the order lifecycle.
